extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, administrative law practitioners, hearing examiners, and policymakers interested in administrative procedure and statistical measurement of proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for the Office of Administrative Procedure's functions and for compiling, defining, and reporting statistics on formal administrative proceedings (APA §11 examiner cases), plus related procedural-improvement activities and evaluative criteria for legislation and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the Office of Administrative Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: With a view to achieving improvements in administrative procedures within the Executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government, the Office shall: (a) carry on continuous studies of the adequacy of the procedures by which Federal departments and agencies determine the rights, duties, and privileges of persons; (b) initiate cooperative effort among the departments and agencies and their respective bars to develop and adopt so far as practicable uniform rules of practice and procedure; (c) collect and publish facts and statistics concerning the procedures of the departments and agencies; (d) assist departments and agencies in the formulation and improvement of their administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office's mandate focuses on procedures for agency rulemaking and adjudication (formal and informal), notice and publication, and judicial review procedures. It should conduct continuous study, recommend uniform rules, compile statistics, and advise agencies; its activity includes liaison, conferences, drafting, and consulting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and limitations of the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority of the Office is to request information pertinent and useful to its proper functions, to consult with agencies and other persons interested in administrative procedures, to organize cooperative efforts among such persons to improve administrative procedures, and to report, advise, and recommend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office has no power to demand, to impose, or to compel; it operates by consultation, cooperation, advice, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation via agency liaison officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of 50 departments and agencies designates a responsible staff officer to maintain official liaison with the Office to provide informal contact and current information relating to agency activities in administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison arrangement provides the Office with up-to-date agency information and facilitates cooperative projects (rules overhaul, drafts, conferences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope definition of 'administrative procedures'
rubrics_metrics.description: The purview of the Office is the whole field of administrative procedures in all executive departments and administrative agencies; in its broad sense, 'administrative procedures' encompasses a wide range of governmental activity, but the Office primarily concerns procedures for agency rulemaking and adjudication and matters incident thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine 'purely administrative' procedures (e.g., visa application recordkeeping) may be more appropriate for management consultants and are generally outside practical Office focus; fundamental questions about agency structure are generally beyond the Office's present scope except as incidental information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria for statistical compilation (APA §11 examiner cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compilation is limited to kinds of administrative proceedings in which (1) opportunity is afforded for hearing before an APA section 11 examiner, and (2) such examiner, in normal course, issues a decision or initial or recommended decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings where evidentiary hearings are conducted by the agency itself or by staff other than APA examiners are not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'proceeding' for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'proceeding' means a matter which in normal course is referred to an examiner for evidentiary hearing, by oral or written presentation, and for recommended or initial decision by him, even though it may be a consolidated proceeding involving more than one petition, application, or complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple claimants or docket numbers are joined into a joint hearing with a single binding decision, it is reported as one 'proceeding.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule for determining when a proceeding is 'commenced' (counting start date)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a procedure contemplates hearing on every petition (e.g., court-style), the proceeding is counted from the date of initial filing; when hearings are only held where issues preclude summary disposition, the proceeding is counted from the date the matter is designated for hearing, entered on the hearing docket, or referred to the office of hearing examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age of proceedings is computed from the commencement date as defined above; this distinction must be applied consistently across agencies and kinds of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting reopened cases as input
rubrics_metrics.description: Input counts include cases which had been closed during the year or prior thereto but were reopened during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopened matters are treated the same as new cases for statistical input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'kinds' or 'types' of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies were asked to assort proceedings into kinds or types according to similarities in scope, function, complexity, relief sought, etc., as well as by statutory authority; the Office uses these agency-provided kinds (with some abbreviation) in its tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification by 'kind' facilitates comparability across similar proceedings but requires agencies to apply consistent characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 metric: Number pending, commenced, and terminated
rubrics_metrics.description: For each agency and kind of proceeding, report number pending at the start of fiscal year, input (new cases commenced plus reopened), output (number of cases closed during the year), and balance pending at end of year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a general view of volume and backlog; used to identify agencies with critical backlogs (e.g., Federal Power Commission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 2 metric: Age of proceedings pending at year-end (age groupings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure age of each pending case from its commencement date and present counts grouped by age ranges (e.g., under 6 months, 6–12 months, 1–2 years, over 3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age groupings are preferred to averages or medians because the variety of administrative proceedings can make scalar averages misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 3 metric: Manner of disposition of proceedings terminated
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize terminations by manner (e.g., final agency decision on the merits after hearing and examiner decision; terminated by default, withdrawal, settlement, or other consent; disposed of by examiner decisions which became final without agency review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows what proportion 'travel the full route' through hearing, examiner decision, and agency final decision; highlights prevalence of dispositions without full hearing or with examiner decisions final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 4 metric: Overall time from commencement to agency final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure overall elapsed time for proceedings that closed by agency final decision on the merits after hearing and examiner decision (from commencement to final decision), reported by time intervals (e.g., under 6 months, 6–12 months, 1–2 years, over 2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess timeliness of full-route adjudicatory processes; excludes time consumed by petitions for reopening, rehearing, or reconsideration (recommended to be measured later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 5 metric: Time from commencement to completion of evidentiary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure elapsed time from the commencement of a proceeding to the date the evidentiary hearing is completed; hearing completion is the last day on which testimony or documentary or other evidence was put into the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interval is one way to measure 'administrative processing' delay before the hearing stage and should be distinguished from assignment-to-examiner timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 6 metric: Time from examiner decision to agency final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the interval from the examiner's initial or recommended decision to the agency's final decision (time under agency review), reported by interval categories and percentage distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights agency deliberation and review lengths; useful for identifying delays in agency decisional processes (e.g., percents over 6 months, over 1 year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 7 metric: Time under advisement by the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the interval from the date the matter was first ripe for agency decision (record certified, oral argument completed, last brief filed, etc.) to the issuance of the agency's final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports distribution of times under advisement (e.g., percent under 1 month, over 6 months, over 1 year) to assess agency decision latency once record is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 8 metric: Hearing examiner proceedings volume and backlog
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings in the hands of hearing examiners, report number pending before examiners at start and end of year, input (new cases assigned to office of hearing examiners and remands/reassignments), examiners' output, and backlog changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows analysis of examiner workload, backlog trends over multiple years, and impact of large caseloads (e.g., Social Security).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 9 metric: Age of hearing examiner cases at year-end
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure age distribution of cases that are or were in the hands of hearing examiners, from assignment-to-examiner (or date turned over to office of hearing examiners) to the report date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps identify aging docket problems within examiner offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 10 metric: Manner of disposition by hearing examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify hearings' terminations by how examiners disposed of proceedings (e.g., examiner decisions, dismissals, settlements during examiner stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the role and finality of examiner-level dispositions separate from agency review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 11 metric: Total time from assignment to examiners to issuance of examiner decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure total elapsed time from the date the proceeding is assigned to the office of hearing examiners to the issuance of the examiner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures full examiner-stage duration (including scheduling, hearings, post-hearing work) and is useful for examiner performance metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 12 metric: Time from assignment to examiners to completion of evidentiary hearing (examiner-stage hearing delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure elapsed time from assignment to the office of hearing examiners to the completion of the evidentiary hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolates scheduling and processing delays within examiner offices prior to hearing completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 13 metric: Time from completion of evidentiary hearing to issuance of examiner decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure elapsed time after hearing completion until the examiner issues a decision, reported by interval categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts for time examiners spend analyzing the record, preparing decision, and receiving post-hearing submissions; note that measurement definitions changed across years (1957/58 measured from last submission to examiner; 1959 measured from hearing completion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 14 metric: Hearing examiner staff productivity and workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Report number of APA §11 examiners employed (man-years), average number of days per man-year in hearings and hearing conferences, average number of examiner decisions per man-year, and total number of proceedings assigned to examiners for conduct of hearings only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate examiner staffing adequacy, productivity (decisions/man-year), and hearing-time burden; footnotes clarify inclusion/exclusion (e.g., default decisions excluded in later years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical limitations and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics involve inherent limitations: varied kinds of proceedings are not identical, definitions and data availability differ across agencies, and some data (e.g., Indian probate, Social Security, ICC) may be incomplete or excluded from grand totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistics intelligently as a tool complementary to detailed study; prefer age groupings over simple averages when variability is large; explicitly annotate exclusions and definitional differences; document changes in measurement methods across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for age groupings over averages in reporting durations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office favors demonstrating age of proceedings by age grouping because this technique is probably more indicative than average or median figures for these varied proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present distributions (counts by age brackets) rather than single-number averages to avoid misleading conclusions caused by heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement guidance for hearing 'completion'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of measuring time to completion of evidentiary hearing, the hearing is considered completed on the last day on which testimony or documentary or other evidence was put into the record, whether or not oral argument on the record was to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition standardizes the endpoint for measuring hearing-stage durations across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority recommendation for time-measurement focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts to measure post-decisional processes (petitions for reopening, rehearing, reconsideration) should be subordinated to measurement of the time it takes to get a final decision in the first instance; post-decision processes may be compiled in subsequent surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial measurement efforts should focus on first-instance adjudicatory timelines (commencement → final decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative review criteria (procedural provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: When commenting on bills or proposed statutes, the Office's interest is confined to whether procedural and judicial review provisions: (a) accord with accepted concepts of due process, (b) will promote fairness, efficiency, and economy, (c) involve unnecessary dissimilarity to other procedures for performance of similar functions, and (d) whether the language is precise and free of ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not comment on the merits of regulatory schemes themselves; its comments are limited to procedural quality and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on rules studies and rulemaking assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office assists agencies in overhauling rules of practice and drafting rules for new proceedings (e.g., under new statutes), and studies specific features of procedural rules when referred by agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work includes drafting language, preparing analyses and suggestions, and conferences with agencies and congressional staff; aim to develop simple, economical, and standard procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of conduct and public information practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office prepares studies and recommendations on standards of conduct for administrative proceedings and on public information practices of Executive agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations may cover conduct during proceedings, public disclosure practices, and the role of public counsel; these are part of projects to improve fairness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project reporting and activity categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office categorizes its completed assignments (e.g., legislative proposals, revision of agency procedural rules, special studies/reports/recommendations, appellate litigation involvement, miscellaneous assignments) and reports counts and types annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking types of projects helps evaluate Office workload and focus (e.g., 52 legislative proposals, 19 rules revisions in 1959).
